title: Special protections for child witnesses during testimony
p1:
A child entering a courtroom is not just a smaller version of an adult witness.

The biggest challenge is often not what the child knows, but whether the legal process allows them to share it safely.
p2:
Many people assume every witness must face the same courtroom experience. That is not always true.

Child witnesses may receive special protections, such as giving evidence through video links, using child-friendly spaces, or having support persons present. These measures help reduce fear and make testimony more reliable.
p3:
The goal is not to give children an unfair advantage. It is to remove unnecessary stress that can affect memory, communication, and confidence.

A simple but powerful idea: justice works better when vulnerable witnesses are protected while still being heard.

Creating a safer environment can help courts discover facts without causing additional harm to the child.
conclusion: Should courts do more to balance a child's emotional safety with the need for fair testimony from all sides?
